title: Fix his posture: chest up, straight back, head over the shoulders

log.text: Starting from the latest run: back rounds 30° / 34° / 41° (should be straight), head 20–21° further forward than the coach at the middle and bottom.
Started: reading the brief, the solver's history and how the Studio measures back rounding and neck angle.
Paused for a while by a usage limit on my side; resuming now from where it stopped.
Built a copy of the character before the posture step (in my scratch folder) so I can measure where the rounded back and forward head come from, joint by joint.

Root cause found. The rounded back has two sources: the Mixamo clip itself already bends his spine 9° standing to 35° at the bottom, and then our posture step reaches the coach's forward lean by bending the spine further (+21° standing, +16° middle, +6° bottom) instead of tipping the hips forward; the hips are never turned. The arm and bar step changes nothing here.

The forward head follows from that: the curled chest carries the base of the neck forward. On this character a neutral head already reads 28° on the Studio's neck measure (his shoulder joints sit 77 mm behind his hip joints), so matching the coach's 13° means tilting the head back about 20° against the chest, which is also what the coach's face direction needs.

First fix tried (spine kept straight, hips tip forward for the lean, neck and head set to the coach's): back rounding 30/34/41° → 0/0/0°, neck vs coach 38.9/15.6/14.2° against 38.6/13.4/13.5°. The face looks up too much in the middle (−2° against the coach's −14°); tuning that next, then looking at the pictures.

Balanced the face against the neck: neck within 4° of the coach at every position, face within 8° (it was 14° off). Starting a full run of the Studio's own squat command in my scratch folder (about 8 minutes).

Full run 1 measured the Studio's way: back rounding 30/34/41° → 0/0/0° (pass at all three), neck 38/34/34° → 39/17/15° against the coach's 39/13/13° (all pass). Two things got worse and must be fixed before I finish: the upper arm at the start is 0.6° outside its tolerance, and two small new skin folds appeared (the neckline on frames 58–59 and the right ankle on frame 38).

Neck fold traced: my first head solve bent the neck bone itself back 24–33° (the old motion never bent it more than 13°), which creases the skin at the back of the neck. Capping the neck bone at 13° and letting the head take the rest brings the neck's largest fold from 542 mm² down to 82 mm² (the Studio's limit is 100); the neck angle still passes (within 5.5° of the coach).

Hips now tip about the line through both hip joints (not a fixed axis), which keeps the two legs as they were relative to each other; the hidden crotch fold at the bottom halves (1,932 → 1,040 mm²). The right-ankle crease at the bottom is driven by matching the coach's 22° lean exactly (at 21° it shrinks to 108 mm², the old run sat at 66); investigating. Starting full run 2.

Full run 2: back rounding −0.1/0.0/0.5°, neck 39/19/17° against the coach's 39/13/13° (all pass), the neck fold is gone and the hidden crotch fold is back to its old size (121 against 100 mm²). The grip width now passes too. Still open: the upper arm at the start (48.5°, limit 46.3°) and the right-ankle crease at the deepest frame (168 mm², limit 100). Looking at the shoulders next.

Upper arm explained: with the old curled back the curl itself opened the arm angle through the rep the way the coach's opens (41° → 52°); with a straight back the elbow stayed near 48° the whole rep. Letting the elbow follow the coach's angle more closely gives 44° / 49–51° / 52° (all within tolerance) and the wrists bend no more than before.

Full run 3: every check that passed before still passes (upper arm 44/51/52° now), back straight and neck within tolerance at all three positions. One thing left: a crease at the front of the right ankle at the deepest frame (168 mm², limit 100; it was 66 before, just under). Trying a smoother skin blend at the ankles, the same treatment the shoulders and hips got in the last task.

Full run 4: the smoother ankle blend removes the ankle crease completely (168 mm² → none), but it let the heel follow the shin a little: foot slide 1.1/1.4 mm → 3.0/4.4 mm (limit 5). Keeping the soles out of that blend next.

Why there was a long gap: a test run did not get stuck in a loop. The Mac went to sleep at 00:49 because its battery was at 1% and woke at 09:44 on the charger; the run used only about 2 minutes of processor time in those 9 hours, and its skin step reports 32,290 s, which is the 32,118 s of sleep plus its normal time. It carried on as soon as the Mac woke and is finishing now; nothing was changed for it.

Full run 5 (soles kept out of the ankle blend): back rounding 0/0/0°, neck 39/19/17° against the coach's 39/13/13°, the ankle crease is gone, feet slide 1.1/1.4 mm again, and every check that passed before still passes. The only visible fold left is the known left-thumb one. Now re-checking the grip, the knees and the old fixes before I finish.

summary: Back rounding 30°/34°/41° → 0°/0°/0.5° (start/middle/end; worst frame of the whole squat 0.5°, was 41°). Neck against the coach (39/13/13°): 38/34/34° → 39/19/17°, all within tolerance now. Checks 16 pass / 11 fail → 21 pass / 6 fail in my test run, nothing that passed before fails; the grip, feet, cracks and smooth motion are unchanged, and the only visible fold is still the known left-thumb one. Still not perfect: at the start he now tips forward from the hips with a straight back (the coach stands more upright), and his face looks a little higher than the coach's in the middle and at the bottom.
